title: Spanner
prompt: A labelled bench teaching model holds a bolt so an open-ended spanner can turn its nut. Turn tightens the nut and Reverse loosens it. Compare lengths exchanges short and long spanners with the same jaw size, applying the same perpendicular hand force at their ends. The longer effort arm gives greater torque. See-through shows the two jaw contact faces, nut flats, bolt axis and thread engagement. Effort arm and torque appear as overlays.
blurb: A bench teaching model uses interchangeable open-ended spanners to turn a nut and compare torque at the same hand force.

identity.note: The Wheel and Axle at Work / Spanner, 2016 page 32. The same example is Wrench in the 1998 edition on page 32.
identity.mechanism: A hand force applied away from the bolt axis creates torque. A longer perpendicular effort arm produces more torque for the same force.
identity.classificationNote: Only The Wheel and Axle and Gears and Belts are main principle chapters in this unit. Other entries are named examples, diagrams or subsection headings. Greek Mill has both historical context and a named mechanism diagram.

adaptationDecision.reason: Retain. Prior pliers uses linked pivoting jaws to grip a rod. This tool transmits torque through nut flats. Its wheel-and-axle chapter placement is supported even though it does not look like a wheel.
adaptationDecision.boundary: Catalog and figure metadata establish intended scope only. No existing figure runtime was certified.

prompt.note: Turning a nut on a restrained bolt is a faithful fixture adaptation of the pictured tool turning a bolt. Make Lengthen handle a swap of real tool lengths. The spanner is a rotating lever, not a hidden geared machine.
prompt.apparatusRelation: Named rotating-lever tool. The restrained bolt and interchangeable spanners are teaching fixtures.

builderTruthNotes: Simple tool. Label handle, head, jaw contact faces, nut, bolt and specimen restraint when drawn. No ratchet or adjustment screw unless separately sourced.

Label all meaningful drawn real components and physical features. Distinguish force and travel overlays from anatomy. The individual builder brief must declare its expected minimum before building. No invented parts to meet a quota.
Identify the teaching adaptation in metadata, blurb and truth notes. Reset, specimen exchange, slow view and hand positioning are teaching controls rather than hidden machine hardware.

teachingAdaptation.fixture: A bench block captures the bolt head while a nut turns on its right-hand thread. A washer receives the nut at the seated limit.
teachingAdaptation.actions: Turn and Reverse are bounded 30 degree hand strokes. Compare lengths exchanges complete equal-jaw tools without changing nut position.
teachingAdaptation.dimensions: 5 drawing units per cm, 24 mm jaw opening, 16 mm nominal bolt and 2 mm pitch; hand force 40 N at 120 or 200 mm.
teachingAdaptation.limits: Rigid ideal contact. Available torque is force times perpendicular arm, not a measured tightening torque or preload. Axial travel is small because pitch is respected.

supplementalSources.supports: Continuous helical threads, matching pitch and diameter, right-hand clockwise tightening.
